identity_comparison: Ethos public archive identifies First Coast and eight other named sites for an age ≥1 year, ≥44 lb, post-amputation randomized canine appendicular OSA vaccine-versus-carboplatin study with up to $4,000 surgical credit and 6–8 months of follow-up. First Coast names its matching ≥1 year/≥20 kg Stage IIB study as K9-ACV + checkpoint inhibitor versus carboplatin, same amputation/randomization and follow-up. Ardent and Unleash identify K9-ACV/CD200AR-L as the exact randomized cohort; the AVMA current object VCT25005864/20869 names this construct and comparator and says Completed. Former sites including CASE, Metropolitan Akron, Massachusetts, Mission, Peak and VSH North County overlap the exact official AVMA announcement. Unleash independently states recruitment complete.

registry.title: Autologous Cancer Vaccine with Checkpoint Inhibitor for Treatment of Canine Osteosarcoma
registry.description: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of K9-ACV, an autologous killed tumor cell vaccine combined with a novel checkpoint inhibitor (CD200AR-L), compared to standard-of-care chemotherapy for the treatment of canine appendicular osteosarcoma (OSA). K9-ACV has safely been used in over 1,000 dogs and the vaccine has been shown to display safety in a previous study (without the addition of the checkpoint inhibitor). By evaluating K9-ACV, this trial aims to advance safer, immune-based treatment options for canine cancer that may offer comparable or superior outcomes to chemotherapy.Participating patients will be required to complete standard pre-enrollment screening that involves a physical exam, blood work, chest x-rays, and abdominal ultrasound. If the patient passes the screening, they will undergo limb amputation and be randomly assigned to the K9-ACV group or the carboplatin group. Patients in the K9-ACV group will receive an intradermal injection of the checkpoint inhibitor and then will return to the study site 24 hours later for the vaccine administration. Vaccines will be given every 3 weeks for a total of 3 treatments. Patients will return at 4, 6, and 8 months after initial vaccine administration for a physical exam, blood work, and x-rays. Patients in the chemotherapy group will be treated every 3 weeks for a total of 4 treatments. Patients will return at 4, 6, and 8 months after initial chemotherapy treatment for a physical exam, blood work, and x-rays.

site_conflict: Current First Coast source still shows Open under Closed Clinical Studies; archived network owner page said Now Enrolling. Neither supersedes exact AVMA Completed and current coordinating sponsor completion under owner rule. No reactivation or assumption of a new cohort.
